2027-04-10.title: Saturday of the Second Week of Easter
readings: They chose seven men full of the Holy Spirit
Lord, let your mercy be on us, as we place our trust in you (or: Alleluia)
They saw Jesus walking on the sea
2027-04-10.alt: Easter weekday of the Second Week of Easter. The Alleluia is sung before the Gospel; the Regina Caeli replaces the Angelus until Pentecost. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-04-10.verse: But he said to them, “It is I; do not be afraid.”
theo: The young Church has its first internal crisis, and it is about food and fairness. The disciples are increasing in number, and “the Hellenists complained against the Hebrews because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution of food.” The Hellenists were Jewish believers who spoke Greek and had come from the lands of the dispersion; the Hebrews spoke Aramaic and belonged to the land. Two cultures in one community, and the poorest, the widows, were falling between them. The apostles do not ignore the complaint or blame anyone. They call the whole community together and propose a solution: “select from among yourselves seven men of good standing, full of the Spirit and of wisdom,” to serve the tables, “while we, for our part, will devote ourselves to prayer and to serving the word.” All seven chosen have Greek names: the community entrusts the care of the neglected to people from the neglected group. The apostles pray and lay their hands on them. The Church has long seen in this scene the beginnings of the diaconate, a ministry of service ordained by the laying on of hands (Catechism 1569–1571). And the result: “The word of God continued to spread… and a great many of the priests became obedient to the faith.” A problem honestly faced became a moment of growth.

In the Gospel, after the feeding of the five thousand, the disciples go down to the sea in the evening and set out by boat for Capernaum. John adds a quiet, heavy sentence: “It was now dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them.” The sea becomes rough with a strong wind. They have rowed three or four miles when they see Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat, “and they were terrified.” Then he speaks: “It is I; do not be afraid.” In Greek it is simply ego eimi, I AM, the name God revealed to Moses at the burning bush. The One who multiplied the loaves is the Lord of creation who walks on the chaos of the waters, as the Psalms say only God can do. When they want to take him into the boat, “immediately the boat reached the land toward which they were going.” The Church has often been pictured as a boat on a dark sea. Today's two readings belong together: in the first, the boat of the Church meets a storm from within, quarrels and neglect; in the second, a storm from outside. In both, the risen Lord comes across the water and says the same words: It is I; do not be afraid.
outline: Ask: what storm is your family or your parish rowing through right now?
Point 1 · The widows who were forgotten
A complaint heard and a problem solved.
Point 2 · Prayer, the word, and service
Point 3 · It is I; do not be afraid
The Lord walks on the dark sea.
“It is I; do not be afraid.”
live: Visit or phone an elderly widow or widower in your parish today, or ask how the parish can help them.
Say his name in the storm (John 6:20)
When fear rises today, stop and pray: Jesus, it is you; I will not be afraid.
2027-04-10.prayer: Lord Jesus, you walked on the stormy sea and said to your frightened disciples: It is I; do not be afraid. Come to us in every storm, from within and from without. Give your Church ministers full of the Spirit and of wisdom, who will care for the forgotten, and keep our pastors faithful to prayer and the service of the word. Let your mercy be on us, as we place our trust in you. Who live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.
altar: The Lord who walks on the waters comes to us in the Eucharist and says: It is I. At the altar, deacon and priest serve the one Bread and the one Word, and the boat of the Church is brought safely to the shore.

quick: The Greek-speaking widows were being neglected, and the apostles listened to the complaint.
Seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom were chosen to serve, and the apostles laid hands on them.
Jesus came walking on the stormy sea and said: It is I; do not be afraid.
2027-04-10.action: Visit, call or help one widow or elderly person living alone this weekend.
2027-04-10.question: Who in my parish or family is being quietly forgotten?

family.explain: The disciples were in a boat at night. The wind was strong, the waves were big, and they were scared. Then they saw Jesus walking on the water! He said: It is I; do not be afraid. As soon as they took him into the boat, they reached the shore.
family.intention: We pray for fishermen at sea tonight, and for all who are afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes us afraid?” Then each one says: Jesus, it is you; I will not be afraid.

illus: A group of fishermen from Vizhinjam were caught in a sudden squall far from the coast one monsoon night. The engine failed and the radio went dead. The oldest of them, who had led the rosary at the harbour chapel for thirty years, made them all hold on to the boat and pray together, aloud, again and again: Jesus, it is you; do not let us be afraid. At dawn a coast guard vessel found them, drifting but alive. Back on shore, he said: the sea did not become calm at once, but we did.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, who walk on the waters, come to us in our storms and speak your word: It is I; do not be afraid. Alleluia. Amen.
share: Their widows were being neglected (Acts 6:1). Whom do I overlook without meaning to?
We will devote ourselves to prayer and to serving the word (Acts 6:4). How can I support my priests and deacons in their ministry?
It was now dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them (John 6:17). Where in my life is it dark and Jesus seems absent?
pm.resp: Lord, let your mercy be on us, as we place our trust in you.
interc: For deacons, priests and bishops, that they may be full of the Spirit and of wisdom.
For widows, the elderly and all who are neglected, that the Church may never forget them.
For communities divided by language or culture, that they may become one family.
For fishermen and all who travel by sea, and for all who are afraid.
For our group, that in every storm we may hear Jesus say: It is I.
pm.close: Father, your Son walks on the stormy sea and brings us safe to shore. Keep us trusting in his presence. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the first Church had a problem. Some widows were being forgotten in the daily distribution of food. The Greek-speaking believers complained. The apostles did not say: everything is fine. They listened, called everyone together and found a solution: seven men full of the Spirit and of wisdom, chosen to serve (Acts 6:3).

Look at the result. The forgotten widows were cared for, the apostles could give themselves to prayer and the word, and the word of God spread. A complaint, when it is heard with humility, can become a grace. Every parish has its forgotten widows. Who are they in ours?

In the Gospel the disciples are rowing at night against a strong wind. John says: it was now dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them (John 6:17). Many of us know that feeling. Then they see Jesus walking on the water, and he says: it is I; do not be afraid (John 6:20). In Greek it is simply: I AM, the name of God.

The storm may come from inside, like the quarrel over the widows, or from outside, like the wind on the sea. In both, the risen Lord comes to us. Today at this altar he comes again, and says: it is I. Let us take him into our boat, and trust that he will bring us to the shore. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, the friends of Jesus were in a boat at night, and a big wind was blowing. They were afraid. Then Jesus came walking on the water and said: It is I; do not be afraid! When you are scared at night, you can say: Jesus, you are with me. I am not afraid!

intro: Theme: “It is I; do not be afraid.”
The forgotten widows, the seven servants, and the Lord who walks on the dark sea.

sub: Care for the neglected entrusted to their own.
q: who executes justice for the orphan and the widow, and who loves the strangers, providing them food and clothing.
Therefore, friends, select from among yourselves seven men of good standing, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint to this task,
points.apply: Find out this week whether any widow or elderly person in your area lacks food, medicine or company, and do something about it.

q: For the word of the LORD is upright, and all his work is done in faithfulness.
while we, for our part, will devote ourselves to prayer and to serving the word.
points.apply: Pray by name for your parish priest and for a deacon you know, and offer to take on one task that frees them for prayer.

points.h: It is I; do not be afraid
sub: Dark, and Jesus not yet come.
q: he made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed. Then they were glad because they had quiet, and he brought them to their desired haven.
Then they wanted to take him into the boat, and immediately the boat reached the land toward which they were going.
points.apply: Write “It is I; do not be afraid” on a card and keep it where you will see it each morning.

concl: A Church that listens to complaints and cares for the forgotten grows in the word of God.
In every storm, from within or without, the risen Lord comes and says: It is I.
2027-04-10.resolve: Visit or call one lonely elderly person every week of Eastertide.
